quizName: Hardest Questions in South carolina Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the side of the operator.

questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold onto their waist or hips. If the motorcycle has handgrips, passengers can hold those instead. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: Why should you check your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To see if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
To watch for pedestrians in front of you.
To check for dark clouds that may mean bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when stopping to make sure drivers behind you see you stopping and are reacting safely.

questions.question: What type of clothing should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to make yourself more visible while riding. Clothing with reflective material also helps.

questions.question: What is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT and state standards gives the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good helmet is the single most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most to you?
questions.explanation: Protection should be your main concern when choosing a helmet.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly, have no cracks, and have no loose padding or frayed straps.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently.

questions.question: What should you know about taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: It is usually safe because over-the-counter drugs are weak.
It is always fine to take.
It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medicines, including over-the-counter drugs, can make it harder to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication may affect your riding ability.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, should you wear a jacket?

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers are most likely to see you.

questions.question: What should you do before riding a borrowed motorcycle?

options.text: Assume the controls are in the same places as your motorcycle.
Take it right out on the highway.
Practice with it in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn where all the controls are and practice in a safe area before riding on the road.

questions.question: What is the only way to become sober after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time will make you sober. Nothing else can speed up how your body removes alcohol.

questions.question: What should matter most when choosing a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection should be your main concern. Choose a helmet that fastens securely, fits correctly, and meets DOT standards.

questions.question: What should you check before every motorcycle ride?

options.text: That your brake lights work properly.
That the paint is not peeling.
That the bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: That your brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test each brake control to make sure the brake lights turn on.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should all riders do?

options.text: Keep a safe distance from each other.
Follow as close together as possible.
Not worry about the distance between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from each other.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. This lets riders stay together while keeping safe distances between them.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent fatigue on a long ride?
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks during long trips to reduce fatigue. Caffeine may make you more tired later when it wears off. Dress warmly and use a windshield to protect yourself from wind and weather, which can increase fatigue.

questions.question: What benefit do reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing provide?

options.text: They should only be worn at night.
They help other drivers see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that makes you visible and keeps space around your motorcycle.
Any position you like, regardless of other vehicles.
One that gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that makes you visible and keeps space around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you and where you have space around your motorcycle. The best position changes as road conditions change. There is no single position that is always right or always wrong.

questions.question: How do you get the most protection from your helmet?
questions.explanation: Get maximum protection by choosing a helmet that meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: To be seen more easily by other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing helps other drivers see you. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol quickly, it builds up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after one hour.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcycle rider:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothing protects you if you crash. It should be comfortable and easy for other drivers to see.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers are dangerous for motorcycles. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that cover your ankles provide the best protection. Laced boots are best. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in before riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Begin slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, making it slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Begin slowing earlier to stop. Also look for bigger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider should constantly watch the road ahead for:
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for changing traffic, dangerous road conditions, and ways to escape danger. Be ready to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about upcoming road hazards. This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead.
